newsitem.title: USA: Mikohn's SafeJack system approved by Nev.
newsitem.headline: Mikohn's SafeJack system approved by Nev.

text.p: Mikohn Gaming Corp said Friday that it received regulatory approval from the Nevada Gaming Control Board for further installations of SafeJack, a system of blackjack management.
This approval followed more than three months of rigorous testing of the system at Bally's on the Las Vegas Strip.

The company also announced that Terrance W. Oliver, 47, recently retired chief operating officer of Fitzgerald's Gaming Corp and member of Mikohn's board of directors since 1988, is spearheading the next phase of development on SafeJack.

The company said it believed that SafeJack had the potential to become "one of the most important technological advances in casino gaming since the introduction of the microprocessor to slot machines. With more than 16,000 blackjack tables -- 8,000 of which are in the U.S.A. -- this is undoubtedly the casino world's most popular table game.

SafeJack contributes not only to the integrity of blackjack and to management information but also offers new dimensions in player tracking and game enhancement. It improves the casino's profitability from blackjack by eliminating most dealer mistakes, common cheating techniques and player disputes, the company said.

Operating with any brand of playing cards and without changing the look and feel of traditional blackjack, SafeJack uses patented computer and sensor technology to electronically track all bets made and cards played in real-time for an accurate record of each game.
